esp32_input_only.fact: GPIO34-39 are input-only: no output driver and no internal pull-up/pull-down.
esp32_input_only.quote: GPIO pins 34-39 are input-only. These pins do not feature an output driver

also.quote: Input only pins, output is not supported due to lack of pull-up/pull-down resistors.

esp32_adc2_wifi.fact: ADC2 is shared with Wi-Fi. In ESP-IDF v4.4 legacy driver, adc2_get_raw() always fails with ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT once Wi-Fi is started. Current IDF oneshot driver arbitrates and adc_oneshot_read() may return ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT.
esp32_adc2_wifi.source: ESP-IDF Programming Guide, ADC (v4.4) and ADC Oneshot Mode Driver (stable)
esp32_adc2_wifi.page_note: Web docs, no page. Not stated in the ESP32 datasheet text.
esp32_adc2_wifi.quote: If Wi-Fi is started via esp_wifi_start(), this function will always fail

also.quote: ADC2 is also used by Wi-Fi.

esp32_strapping_pins.fact: Strapping pins GPIO0, GPIO2 (boot mode), MTDI=GPIO12 (VDD_SDIO voltage), MTDO=GPIO15 (U0TXD printing, SDIO timing), GPIO5 (SDIO timing) are latched at reset. Defaults: GPIO0 pull-up, GPIO2 pull-down, MTDI pull-down, MTDO pull-up, GPIO5 pull-up.
esp32_strapping_pins.quote: Chip boot mode – Strapping pin: GPIO0 and GPIO2

also.note: Pin table maps MTDI=GPIO12, MTDO=GPIO15; page 23 Table 3-3 Chip Boot Mode Control.

atmega328p_pin_current.fact: Absolute max DC current per I/O pin is 40.0 mA; DC characteristics are specified at test condition IOL/IOH = 20 mA at VCC = 5 V (10 mA at 3 V).

also.quote: sink more than the test conditions (20mA at VCC = 5V, 10mA at VCC = 3V)
also.note: 20 mA test condition found in Table 30-1 (TA -40 to 105 C), pages 322-323; the 40 mA rating also appears on page 322. Ch.29 (-40 to 85 C) common DC table text not extracted.

hcsr04_specs.fact: Range 2 cm-400 cm; trigger is a 10 us high pulse; use over 60 ms measurement cycle.
hcsr04_specs.source: ElecFreaks HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Ranging Module sheet (SparkFun-hosted), 3 pages
hcsr04_specs.quote: HC - SR04 provides 2cm - 400cm non-contact measurement function

also.quote: we suggest to use over 60ms measurement cycle
also.note: Page 1 also: 'Trigger Input Signal 10uS TTL pulse'. PDF page index; sheet has no printed page numbers.

dht22_sampling_period.fact: Sensing period average 2 s; collecting period should be > 2 s between reads.

dht22_pullup.fact: Data line needs a pull-up to VDD. The AM2302 sheet's connection diagram shows a 1K pull-up (value appears only inside the diagram image, not in text). The SparkFun DHT22 sheet's diagram (p5) is cropped and shows no resistor value.
dht22_pullup.quote: 1K (label on pull-up resistor in '5. Electrical connection diagram')
dht22_pullup.page_note: Confirmed visually by rendering page 2; common 4.7k-10k advice is NOT in either sheet.

mpu6050_i2c_addr.fact: 7-bit I2C address b110100X: 0x68 when AD0 low, 0x69 when AD0 high.
mpu6050_i2c_addr.source: InvenSense MPU-6000/MPU-6050 Product Specification PS-MPU-6000A-00 Rev 3.1 (SparkFun mirror; TDK URL returned HTML)
mpu6050_i2c_addr.quote: the address of the one of the devices should be b1101000 (pin AD0 is logic

also.note: Hex conversion (0x68/0x69) is derived; datasheet gives binary.

pcf8574_vs_a_addr.fact: PCF8574 address 0100 A2A1A0 = 0x20-0x27; PCF8574A address 0111 A2A1A0 = 0x38-0x3F. LCD1602 backpacks with A2-A0 pulled high default to 0x27 (PCF8574) or 0x3F (PCF8574A).
pcf8574_vs_a_addr.source: TI PCF8574 datasheet SCPS068K (rev. Sept 2024); TI PCF8574A datasheet SCPS069H (rev. Sept 2024)
pcf8574_vs_a_addr.quote: I2C target address L H L L A2 A1 A0 R/W

also.quote: S 0 1 1 1 A2 A1 A0 (Figure 6-3, I2C Write Voltage Waveforms)
also.note: PCF8574 sheet p10 shows 'S 0 1 0 0 A2 A1 A0'. Hex ranges and 0x27/0x3F backpack defaults are derived, not printed. NXP combined PCF8574/74A PDF could not be downloaded (returned HTML).

sg90_pwm.fact: Pulse cycle about 20 ms (= 50 Hz); ~1 ms to ~2 ms pulse (1.5 ms middle); operating voltage 4.8-6.0 V.
sg90_pwm.source: SG90 datasheet compilation (friendlywire.com, 7 pages: TowerPro-style sheet + vendor spec pages)

pages.1: Position "0" (1.5 ms pulse) is middle, "90" (~2ms pulse)

also.note: '50 Hz' not printed in text; derived from 20 ms. Page 2 lists pulse width 500-2400 us; page 1 says 4.8 V (~5V). Imperial College copy of the classic TowerPro sheet timed out.

arduino_pulsein_timeout.fact: Optional timeout is in microseconds; default is one second. Returns 0 on timeout.
arduino_pulsein_timeout.source: Arduino Language Reference: pulseIn() (verified from reference-en source pulseIn.adoc)
arduino_pulsein_timeout.page_note: Web page, no page number. Text read from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arduino/reference-en/master/Language/Functions/Advanced%20IO/pulseIn.adoc because docs page is client-rendered.
arduino_pulsein_timeout.quote: the number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second.

_meta.page_convention: page = 1-based PDF page index. Checked equal to printed page for ESP32 (footer), ATmega (DS40002061B-page N), MPU (N of 57), TI (footer), DHT22 SparkFun p5. HC-SR04, AM2302 and SG90 compilation use PDF index.
